Story: As a user, I can sign in once and access applications available to my membership.
Acceptance criteria:
Session establishes user and active tenant server-side.
Disabled membership is rejected at the service boundary.
Signing out removes access to protected Genie views.

Story: As an administrator, I can invite, deactivate and manage workspace members.
Acceptance criteria:
Only authorized administrators can change membership.
Deactivation blocks new reads and mutations.
Membership changes are auditable.

Story: As an administrator, I can grant roles with explicit resource and action permissions.
Acceptance criteria:
Read and mutation permissions are distinct.
Role changes apply to UI, tools and background execution.
A user cannot grant a permission they are unauthorized to manage.

Story: As a multi-workspace user, I can explicitly switch my active workspace.
Acceptance criteria:
Active workspace is visible.
Conversations and resource search remain tenant-scoped.
Pending jobs retain their original tenant context.

Story: As an administrator, I can revoke access before pending actions execute.
Acceptance criteria:
Permissions are rechecked at mutation time.
Revoked actions stop without exposing inaccessible content.
Denied actions are recorded without sensitive payload leakage.

Story: As a user, I can follow a generated task to its source document.
Acceptance criteria:
Stable source identifiers are recorded.
Following the link checks current access.
Inaccessible source titles are not exposed through backlinks.

Story: As a user, I can distinguish manual changes from Genie actions.
Acceptance criteria:
Activity identifies requester and execution source.
Each automated mutation references its workflow.
Activity does not imply an unexecuted proposal changed data.

Story: As a user, I can inspect linked tasks, events and documents.
Acceptance criteria:
Links are visible only under current authorization.
Deleted targets have a clear unavailable state.
Links use stable resource identifiers.

Story: As a user, I receive useful workflow completion notifications.
Acceptance criteria:
Notification reflects actual terminal state.
Retry does not duplicate the same completion alert.
Notification preferences are respected.

Story: As a member, I can create a project with a name, description and access settings.
Acceptance criteria:
Required fields are validated.
Creation respects workspace permissions.
Project appears in authorized lists after creation.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a member, I can create a task with title, description, status, owner and due date.
Acceptance criteria:
Owner is an eligible member.
Date-only deadlines remain distinct from event timestamps.
UI and tool requests enforce identical field rules.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a member, I can view tasks in list or board views and filter them.
Acceptance criteria:
Filters apply to authorized tasks only.
Owner, status and due-date filters compose correctly.
Empty and failed states are distinguishable.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As an owner, I can update and complete a task.
Acceptance criteria:
Invalid transitions are rejected.
Concurrent updates do not silently overwrite newer state.
Changes retain actor and time.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a collaborator, I can comment on tasks and review activity.
Acceptance criteria:
Only authorized collaborators can comment.
Activity identifies the actor.
Comment failures preserve recoverable user input.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a manager, I can define task dependencies and identify blocked work.
Acceptance criteria:
Dependency targets are accessible.
Self-dependency and forbidden cycles are rejected.
Blocked status is distinguishable from completion status.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a user, I can ask Genie for overdue or upcoming tasks.
Acceptance criteria:
Queries use current user timezone and ownership scope.
Only authorized tasks are returned.
Results link to supporting task records.

Story: As a user, I can review tasks extracted from notes before creation.
Acceptance criteria:
Preview contains exact proposed fields.
Unresolved owners or projects require clarification.
Created tasks use stable operation keys.

Story: As a user, I can request a change to a specific task through Genie.
Acceptance criteria:
Ambiguous tasks require clarification.
Preview shows affected fields.
Execution rechecks current task version and permission.

Story: As a manager, I can obtain a project summary grounded in accessible tasks.
Acceptance criteria:
Claims have resource references where applicable.
Recorded facts are separated from inferred risks.
Summary states its reporting period.

Story: As a manager, I can review updates to several tasks before applying them.
Acceptance criteria:
Batch size is bounded.
Each affected task is included in approval.
Partial failures identify individual outcomes.

Story: As a user, I can create, edit and save a document.
Acceptance criteria:
Save state is visible.
Failures do not silently discard input.
Document has a stable identifier and version reference.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a user, I can share a document at supported access levels.
Acceptance criteria:
Only permitted actors change sharing.
Read and edit permissions differ.
Revocation is enforced by content APIs.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a user, I can select text for Genie context.
Acceptance criteria:
Selection includes document ID and version.
Empty selection is explicit.
Submitted selection does not change after navigation.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a user, I can inspect and recover earlier document content.
Acceptance criteria:
Version access respects current permissions.
Restore creates an auditable revision.
User can preview the restore target.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a collaborator, I can comment on document content.
Acceptance criteria:
Comment anchors retain source references.
Deleted anchors have a visible fallback.
Comment access follows document permissions.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a collaborator, I can edit alongside others without losing changes.
Acceptance criteria:
Conflict-resolution behavior is defined.
Disconnect and reconnect preserve reconciled edits.
Collaboration load is tested separately from ordinary API load.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a user, I can summarize selected text or a specified document.
Acceptance criteria:
Selection takes precedence when intended.
Summary identifies source scope.
Oversized input is bounded or asks for narrower scope.

Story: As a user, I can extract decisions and action items from notes.
Acceptance criteria:
Decisions and proposals are distinguished.
Missing owners and dates remain unresolved.
Source content cannot authorize tools.

Story: As a user, I can review a rewrite before applying it.
Acceptance criteria:
Preview shows affected passage.
No silent overwrite is allowed.
Changed source version triggers revalidation.

Story: As a user, I can ask document questions and inspect supporting passages.
Acceptance criteria:
Answers reference supporting passages.
Unsupported claims are acknowledged.
Current source permissions are checked before retrieval.

Story: As a user, I can create a draft from authorized project information.
Acceptance criteria:
Only authorized sources contribute.
Generated draft is editable.
Creation links relevant sources without leaking inaccessible metadata.

Story: As a user, I can view events in my configured timezone.
Acceptance criteria:
Stored times are unambiguous.
Timezone changes preserve event instants.
All-day events remain date-based.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a user, I can create, edit and cancel personal events.
Acceptance criteria:
Calendar write access is enforced.
Cancellation state is visible.
Provider failures are not shown as success.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a user, I can specify working hours and scheduling preferences.
Acceptance criteria:
Timezone is stored with preferences.
Invalid ranges are rejected.
Preferences do not imply permission to schedule automatically.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As an organizer, I can invite participants and inspect responses.
Acceptance criteria:
Recipients are visible before sending invitations.
Responses map to the correct event.
Private blocks are distinguished from invitations.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a user, I can manage recurring events.
Acceptance criteria:
Single occurrence and whole-series edits are distinct.
Exceptions retain correct dates.
Series changes require an explicit scope choice.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

Story: As a user, I can ask for available slots in a date range.
Acceptance criteria:
Date range resolves in user timezone.
Missing duration triggers clarification.
Unknown participant availability is explicit.

Story: As a user, I can approve a focus block linked to a task.
Acceptance criteria:
Preview shows exact start, end and calendar.
Availability is rechecked before creation.
Task deadlines do not automatically authorize blocks.

Story: As an organizer, I can approve an event and attendee list before invitations.
Acceptance criteria:
Approval includes recipients and event details.
Material attendee edits invalidate approval.
Unauthorized calendars cannot be selected.

Story: As a user, I can request a rescheduling proposal.
Acceptance criteria:
Original event is identified unambiguously.
Conflicts are shown before mutation.
Only the approved occurrence or series is changed.

Story: As a user, I can connect and disconnect a supported mailbox.
Acceptance criteria:
Provider permissions are explicit.
Tokens remain server-side.
Disconnect prevents new access and applies retention policy.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; mailbox hosting excluded

Story: As a user, I can view synchronized messages and threads.
Acceptance criteria:
Only permitted mailbox content appears.
Sync freshness is visible.
Provider errors have recoverable states.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; mailbox hosting excluded

Story: As a user, I can compose and save drafts.
Acceptance criteria:
Drafts remain editable.
Save failures preserve recoverable input.
Retries do not create duplicate drafts.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; mailbox hosting excluded

Story: As a user, I can review and manually send email.
Acceptance criteria:
Recipients and content are visible.
Sending differs from saving a draft.
Uncertain provider outcomes are reconciled before retry.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; mailbox hosting excluded

Story: As a user, I can recover synchronization failures.
Acceptance criteria:
Reconnect preserves existing resource identity.
Revoked provider permission is reported accurately.
Recovery does not request unnecessary broader scopes.
Scope: Existing application prerequisite; mailbox hosting excluded

Story: As a user, I can summarize a selected thread.
Acceptance criteria:
Only the authorized selected thread is read.
Commitments and suggestions are distinguished.
Summary references its source.

Story: As a user, I can draft a reply using authorized project context.
Acceptance criteria:
Recipients come from verified data or user input.
Draft remains editable.
No agent send tool is available initially.

Story: As a user, I can propose tasks from an email commitment.
Acceptance criteria:
Destination project is verified.
Preview retains source reference.
Creation requires approval and duplicate protection.

Story: As a user, I can review a project update draft before manually sending.
Acceptance criteria:
Reporting period is explicit.
Workspace claims are grounded in accessible records.
Draft creation never implies sending.

Story: As a user, I can open Genie from any supported application.
Acceptance criteria:
Entry point is consistently available.
Keyboard navigation is supported.
Inference failure does not hide manual app controls.

Story: As a user, I can see the resource Genie will use.
Acceptance criteria:
Source app and resource are displayed.
User can correct context before submitting.
Inaccessible metadata is omitted.

Story: As a user, I can continue a conversation after changing apps.
Acceptance criteria:
History persists within its authorized scope.
Submitted jobs keep captured context.
New requests clearly show their new context.

Story: As a user, I can inspect, change and delete saved preferences.
Acceptance criteria:
Preferences differ from approval records.
Changes affect subsequent requests.
Deletion propagates to applicable derived memory.

Story: As a user, I can express a supported outcome naturally.
Acceptance criteria:
Routing selects a registered workflow or clarification.
Equivalent phrases map to the same contract.
Unsupported actions do not fabricate tools.

Story: As a user, I receive focused clarification for missing inputs.
Acceptance criteria:
Only unresolved required fields are requested.
Ambiguous people and projects are not guessed.
Answers update the pending plan without mutations.

Story: As an operator, I can restrict each workflow's tools and limits.
Acceptance criteria:
Only relevant tool schemas enter the prompt.
Input and output pass schema validation.
Context, model calls, action count and runtime have bounds.

Story: As a user, I receive a clear unsupported-action response.
Acceptance criteria:
No unauthorized side effects occur.
Response explains the supported alternative where available.
Unsupported requests do not enter unbounded planning loops.

Story: As a user, I can review exact proposed changes.
Acceptance criteria:
Preview shows target resources and field values.
External consequences are explicit.
Approval binds to a plan version.

Story: As a user, I can edit or reject a proposal.
Acceptance criteria:
Rejected plans do not execute.
Material edits invalidate previous approval.
A new preview reflects accepted edits.

Story: As a user, I can see individual action results.
Acceptance criteria:
Success requires an execution receipt.
Partial completion identifies successful and failed steps.
Results link only to accessible resources.

Story: As a user, I can retry failed steps safely.
Acceptance criteria:
Successful actions are not repeated.
Unknown outcomes are reconciled first.
Retry respects current permission and expiry.

Story: As a user, I can cancel pending actions.
Acceptance criteria:
Pending steps stop where cancellable.
Completed changes remain visible.
Cancellation does not promise unsupported rollback.

Story: As a user, I want relevant selected content used directly.
Acceptance criteria:
Known source is fetched without unnecessary semantic search.
Selection scope is preserved.
Source version accompanies the content.

Story: As an operator, I want structured facts fetched from application services.
Acceptance criteria:
Permissions and current state come from authoritative services.
Model output cannot replace access checks.
Queries request necessary fields only.

Story: As an operator, I can bound prompt context.
Acceptance criteria:
History and source content have budgets.
Omission does not silently claim full-source analysis.
Large inputs trigger supported narrowing or explicit processing policy.

Story: As a user, I want stale plans detected before execution.
Acceptance criteria:
Relevant source versions are compared.
Conflicts produce refresh or clarification.
A refresh requiring material changes renews approval.

Story: As a user, I can find resources by names and keywords.
Acceptance criteria:
Search respects tenant and resource access.
Exact references remain usable.
Empty results differ from service failure.

Story: As a user, I can find relevant passages with different wording.
Acceptance criteria:
Semantic retrieval is evaluated against representative queries.
Returned context is bounded.
Permissions are enforced before content reaches the model.

Story: As a user, I can inspect sources supporting an answer.
Acceptance criteria:
Passages retain resource and version references.
Unavailable evidence is not invented.
Source links check current access.

Story: As an administrator, I can remove deleted or restricted content from retrieval.
Acceptance criteria:
Deletion covers chunks and applicable derived summaries.
Permission revocation prevents access despite index lag.
Index freshness and purge failures are observable.

Story: As a user, my accepted request survives disconnect.
Acceptance criteria:
Job is persisted before acceptance.
Job status can be reopened.
Repeated submission identity does not duplicate mutations.

Story: As an operator, workers reconcile interrupted jobs.
Acceptance criteria:
Restart tests recover accepted work.
In-flight actions are reconciled before retry.
No inference wait holds a database transaction open.

Story: As a user, I can distinguish progress and terminal outcomes.
Acceptance criteria:
Queued, planning, approval, execution and terminal states differ.
Partial results survive refresh.
UI never equates generated text with completed action.

Story: As an operator, I can bound retries and expiry.
Acceptance criteria:
Transient and permanent errors differ.
Attempt limits and deadlines are enforced.
Expired actions cannot execute unnoticed.

Story: As an operator, I can enforce tenant and global quotas.
Acceptance criteria:
Limits apply before inference.
One tenant cannot consume the entire queue.
Quota errors explain when retry is useful.

Story: As an operator, I reserve estimated cost before inference.
Acceptance criteria:
Reservations include in-flight work.
Usage reconciliation adjusts reservations.
Safety headroom accounts for estimation error.

Story: As an administrator, I can inspect workflow usage and cost.
Acceptance criteria:
Estimated and reconciled figures are distinguished.
Failed and retried usage is included.
Access to tenant reports is restricted.

Story: As a user, I receive a clear capacity response.
Acceptance criteria:
Queue depth and request expiry are bounded.
Overload does not create unlimited jobs.
Provider unavailability is not presented as a user error.

Story: As a user, I can keep using apps during AI downtime.
Acceptance criteria:
Manual CRUD does not depend on inference.
Inference kill switch prevents new paid work.
Pending workflow status remains readable.

Story: As an engineer, I evaluate representative workflows before release.
Acceptance criteria:
Dataset covers successful, ambiguous and unsupported requests.
Correctness and latency results are recorded.
A model or prompt change reruns affected evaluations.

Story: As an engineer, I test malicious document and email instructions.
Acceptance criteria:
Source text cannot expand tool access.
Cross-tenant negative tests prevent disclosure.
External communication approval cannot be bypassed.

Story: As an operator, I investigate failures through redacted traces.
Acceptance criteria:
Secrets and unnecessary content are excluded.
Traces connect workflow and tool attempts.
Audit access and retention are explicit.

Story: As an engineer, I compare model choices by useful outcomes.
Acceptance criteria:
Compare cost per successful workflow.
Use the same workload for comparisons.
GPU allocation and startup costs are included.

Story: As an administrator, I can audit automated mutations.
Acceptance criteria:
Record includes requester, tenant, approval, tool and result.
Unexecuted proposals remain distinguishable.
Sensitive trace access is restricted.

Story: As an operator, I can rotate webhook secrets without exposing them.
Acceptance criteria:
Credentials remain server-side.
Logs omit authorization values.
Invalid credentials are rejected before expensive inference.

Story: As an administrator, I can apply retention and deletion policies.
Acceptance criteria:
Policy covers conversations, sources, derived content and audit exceptions.
Deletion state is observable.
Backups follow documented retention boundaries.

Story: As an administrator, I can define permitted delegated actions.
Acceptance criteria:
Policy specifies resources, tools, limits and expiry.
Policy cannot exceed actor permissions.
External sends and destructive actions remain separately governed.

Story: As a user, I can inspect and revoke my delegation policies.
Acceptance criteria:
Active scopes are visible.
Revocation affects pending execution.
Changes are audited.

Story: As a product owner, I can register each remaining application's scope.
Acceptance criteria:
Name, users and entities are specified.
Manual prerequisites and agent capabilities are separate.
No capabilities are invented for unspecified apps.

Story: As an engineer, I can implement a connector against its approved contract.
Acceptance criteria:
Tools define schemas, ACLs, limits, approval and recovery.
Context identifies resource and version.
Connector passes isolation and duplicate tests.
